title: Linear space versus quasilinear multitape time
formal:
Does there exist a language decidable in deterministic linear space that has no deterministic quasilinear-time decider on a multitape Turing machine?

With \(n\) denoting binary input length, the precise target is
\[\exists L\in\mathrm{DSPACE}(n),\qquad L\notin\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}}\mathrm{DTIME}\!\left((n+2)\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil^k\right).\]
This is the explicit linear-space, polylogarithmic-overhead instance of Fortnow’s broader direction of separating memory from roughly comparable time. The source does not itself fix this formula or the machine model. The selected multitape formulation has an affirmative published resolution in Williams’s 2025 time-to-space simulation results.
why: The question isolates a basic advantage of reusable memory over a comparable amount of computation. The now-known multitape separation was a substantial step beyond earlier logarithmic-factor gaps and clarifies a weaker frontier underlying P versus PSPACE. Its resolution also illustrates why precise machine and overhead conventions matter for quantitative complexity statements.

definitions:
A language is a subset \(L\subseteq\{0,1\}^*\). All machines here are uniform deterministic multitape Turing machines with a fixed finite program, a read-only two-way input tape and a fixed finite number of work tapes over fixed finite alphabets, initially blank. At one step, each head reads a symbol, a bounded number of work symbols can be written, and each head moves at most one cell. A machine halts in an accept or reject state and must decide membership exactly on every binary string. There is no randomness, nondeterminism, oracle, advice, quantum memory or unit-cost random-access register primitive. The number of tapes and their finite alphabets may depend on the machine, not on input length.

Time is the number of machine steps before halting. Space is the total number of work-tape cells visited, multiplied by a fixed bit width for tape symbols. All stored indices, counters and temporary data count. The input is read-only and is not charged as writable space; the finite control and final one-bit halting answer are also uncharged. Giving the machine a writable copy of the input changes the linear-space bound by only a linear term and the quasilinear time bound by only linear work, so this convention agrees with the relevant multitape classes in the resolution source.

Membership in \(\mathrm{DSPACE}(n)\) means that there are a decider \(A\) for \(L\) and a fixed constant \(c>0\) with
\[\forall x\in\{0,1\}^*,\qquad \operatorname{space}_A(x)\le c(|x|+2).\]
There is no separate runtime requirement on \(A\), beyond halting on every input. Membership in \(\mathrm{DTIME}(t(n))\) means that some decider \(B\) and constant \(c>0\) satisfy \(\operatorname{time}_B(x)\le c\,t(|x|)\) on every input. There is no separate space restriction on \(B\).

Quasilinear time means a bound \(c(n+2)\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil^k\) for some fixed nonnegative integer \(k\) and constant \(c>0\). The exponent and constant may vary among candidate deciders, but not with an individual input. Thus the required single language \(L\) must defeat every such pair of constants and every correct decider. Equivalently, for every correct decider \(B\), every \(k\ge0\), every positive integer \(c\) and every integer \(N\ge0\), there is a string \(x\) of length at least \(N\) with
\[\operatorname{time}_B(x)>c(|x|+2)\lceil\log_2(|x|+2)\rceil^k.\]
This is failure of a worst-case quasilinear bound, not a runtime lower bound on every input. A different language for each \(k\) would not by itself establish the displayed single-language target.

The question compares two computational classes; it does not ask for a tradeoff holding within a particular fixed algorithm or for simultaneous small time and space. A negative answer would put every deterministic linear-space language in quasilinear time, allowing a different decider and logarithmic exponent for each language. The problem does not assert \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{PSPACE}\), which would require ruling out every polynomial time exponent for an appropriate space-bounded language.
answer_criterion: A complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the displayed separation must specify or establish one language with a linear-space decider and prove that it has no quasilinear-time multitape decider with any fixed logarithmic exponent. A refutation would prove the reverse class containment. The published result records the affirmative mathematical status; it does not mean that a Lean proof has already been supplied. A result limited to one-tape machines, a lower bound only for one fixed logarithmic overhead, or a statement about a different random-access cost model would not alone meet this criterion.

context_blocks.text: Fortnow presents this as one of the weaker separations that remained difficult even before resolving P versus NP. His short conclusion does not specify a function or a machine model. This review records the natural linear-space versus quasilinear-multitape instance as an editorial specification, preserving the broader wording in provenance.

Williams proves that deterministic multitape time \(t(n)\ge n\) can be simulated in space \(O(\sqrt{t(n)\log t(n)})\). Corollary 1.2 gives a polynomial separation between space and time, and Corollary 1.3 identifies one language with near-quadratic time lower bounds. These consequences cover the quasilinear-time exclusion in this card.

The article’s introduction calls this a first generic polynomial time-space separation for the multitape model. Remark 1.6 explains that its simulation is not established for arbitrary random-access computations. The archival disposition is limited to the explicit model here and does not claim that every interpretation of the broad survey direction is solved.
